questions.text: Why is it that, in the inset of Fig. 4.4, the mobility is seen to increase with an increase of temperature in a certain temperature range, yet decreases with an increase of temperature in another temperature range?

An electric field applied to a bar of extrinsic GaAs causes equal electron and hole densities. Determine a) The equilibrium electron and hole densities. b) The net doping density.

A semiconductor has an intrinsic resistivity of \( 3 \	imes 10^4 \) ohm-cm. Donor and acceptor atoms are added with densities of \( 10^{14} \) cm⁻³ and \( 5 \	imes 10^{12} \) cm⁻³ respectively. Given \( \mu_n = 1600 \) and \( \mu_p = 600 \) cm²/V-s, determine the current density if the applied electric field is 100mV/cm.

A bar of intrinsic semiconductor has a resistance of 5 ohms at 360K and 50 ohms at 330K. Assume that the change in resistance is a result of the change in \( n_i \) only. Calculate the band gap energy of the semiconductor.
A certain silicon sample has \( N_A = 5.01 \	imes 10^{16} \) cm⁻³ and \( N_D = 5.02 \	imes 10^{16} \) cm⁻³. Given \( \mu_n = 1200 \) and \( \mu_p = 400 \) cm²/V-s, determine

A silicon bar has a length of 1cm, a height of 0.01cm, and a depth of 0.2cm. At T = 300K, determine the resistance of the bar for the following conditions: a) Intrinsic. b) A donor doping of 10^{15}cm^{-3}. c) An acceptor doping of 10^{15}cm^{-3}.

a) For minimum conductivity of a semiconductor sample, determine an expression for the electron and hole density, at a given temperature, in terms of \mu_n, \mu_p, and the intrinsic carrier density. b) Use \mu_n = 3900, \mu_p = 1800 \, cm^{2}/V-s, and n_i = 10^{10}cm^{-3} to calculate the hole density and the maximum resistivity.
Given a Ge sample that has, at a given temperature, n_i = 2.5 × 10^{13}cm^{-3}, \mu_n = 3900 \, cm^{2}/V-s, determine: a) The intrinsic conductivity. b) The minimum conductivity.

Given a semiconductor that has a mobility ratio that is independent of impurity density given by K = \frac{\mu_n}{\mu_p} and K > 1, determine an expression for the maximum resistivity in terms of K and the intrinsic resistivity.

For an electron starting from rest at the first contact, determine: a) The drift velocity of an electron if the space between the contacts is occupied by an N-semiconductor having \mu_n = 3900 \, cm^{2}/V-s. b) The velocity of an electron at a distance of 1cm if the space between the contacts is a vacuum.
A bar of N-type silicon 1cm long is doped with 10^{15}cm^{-3} of donor atoms at T = 300K and a voltage of 5V is applied to the ends of the bar. Determine: a) The hole drift current density.
Determine the steady-state excess hole density at x = 0.
Repeat part (a) at x = 100μm.
Determine the rate of generation of electron-hole pairs at x = 100μm.
Determine the rate of recombination of electron-hole pairs at x = 100μm.

answers.text: At low temperatures, lattice vibrations are so small that as the temperature increases, the carriers receive thermal energy that increases their velocity, thus reducing the time that the electron spends in the vicinity of the lattice and impurity atoms. This reduces the scattering cross section, which causes the mobility to increase with temperature. The increase of mobility with temperature continues until, at a certain temperature, the lattice vibrations dominate and the scattering cross section increases, thus increasing the possibility of collision with the lattice and decreasing the mobility with an increase of temperature.

symbols.description: Representa a densidade de elétrons livres em um semicondutor, que são os portadores de carga negativa.
Representa a densidade de lacunas em um semicondutor, que são os portadores de carga positiva resultantes da ausência de elétrons.

symbols.description: Representa a variação da densidade de elétrons, ou seja, a diferença entre a densidade de elétrons atual e a densidade de elétrons em equilíbrio térmico.
